title: Telling the Time (KS1)
subject: Maths
strapline: O'clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to.
facts: A clock face has 12 numbers; the short hand shows the hour, the long hand shows the minutes.
When the long hand points to 12, it is something o'clock.
When the long hand points to 6, it is half past the hour.
When the long hand points to 3, it is quarter past; pointing to 9 is quarter to.
There are 60 minutes in an hour and 24 hours in a day.
The long (minute) hand moves all the way round once every hour.
"Quarter to 4" means it is 15 minutes before 4 o'clock.

quick_quiz.q: Where does the long hand point at half past?
How many minutes are in one hour?
The long hand points to 3, short hand just past 2. What time is it?

teacher_tips: Use a geared teaching clock so the hour hand moves realistically with the minutes.
Anchor times to the child's day (lunch, home time) to give them meaning.
Teach o'clock and half past thoroughly before quarter past/to.
